column1: # Minecraft Dungeons II (Switch update 1.1.3.0 over a sparse base game), SDK 20.5.15, Unreal Engine 5 (desktop SF_GLSL_SWITCH renderer, IoStore), NVN, Wwise, Havok.
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile; brought up on the Mac with tex_dyn_slots added. The engine allocator cut and the capped engine region below
# were made on Windows from the 2026-11-18 iPad crash (2026-11-20).
# Unreal Engine 5: nninitStartup (main+0x13f30) reserves one engine region with nn::os::AllocateAddressRegion (main+0x14390), 62 GB unless
# -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= caps it (main+0x141f4: up to 4095 it is MB, above that bytes), and exits with exit(1) when the region is refused
# (main+0x143e0: on the iPad the log showed "SVC 0x7" = ExitProcess, then an abort). Then it constructs its FMallocBinned3 in place on main+0x997e228
# (bss; main+0x143b0 → main+0xb0560), which carves 38 GB out of that region (main+0xb0650 → main+0x14964). The constructor call is cut (patches.py)
# and the host runs the engine heap on a malloc zone (hle_uemalloc.c, layout UE5_6, as FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE). The rest of the region is the engine's
# own page allocator: 6 GB in an 8 GB alias region (the SDK's node area takes up to 1 GB at its start). Address space only: nothing is mapped until used.
# the NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource
# the decoded shader code archives: the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 in the check boot: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# 2 particle vertex shaders (210d8abb3b9996c5, d1c8e612ec7462b6) pick a buffer texture at run time: their only c2 reads are texture table words 0x170-0x188 and sampler table words 0x568 / 0x578
# The game's config sets rhi.SyncInterval 2 (30 fps) and t.MaxFPS 0 (no limit), and its bUseFixedFrameRate is off: the engine steps by the time that really passed, so the
# interval the host writes is all 60 and 120 need.
